shoulder_abd.source: AmpAinSoc Reverse Pec Deck: "Adjust the seat so the handles align with your shoulders when seated" and the pause comes "when arms are fully extended back"; no exact top angle is given, so 90 degrees (arms level with the shoulders) is illustrative; 20 degrees is the illustrative starting cross-body reach

elbow_flex.source: AmpAinSoc Reverse Pec Deck: "Slight bend in elbows (10-15 degrees), maintained throughout"

shrug_cm.source: FitnessVolt Reverse Pec Deck: a seat set too low "can turn the path into a high pull and encourage shrugging," so the seat height itself (not a separate cue) is what keeps the shoulders down

muscles.peakSource: AmpAinSoc Reverse Pec Deck: "1-second pause when arms are fully extended back. Squeeze the rear delts," so effort is highest through that hold

mistake.name: Shrug and swing

tells.text: The shoulders creep up toward the ears as the seat sits too low.
The arms jerk past shoulder height on momentum instead of a controlled squeeze.

mistake.source: FitnessVolt Reverse Pec Deck: "Setting the seat too low: This can turn the path into a high pull and encourage shrugging"; "Using too much weight: Momentum, shortened range, and elbow movement usually appear before the target muscles receive better training"

sources: Contact fact (D-FG7 (d), back view): the pattern table already gives horizontal_abduction the back view (rig/patterns.ts); the chest stays against the pad throughout, per Garage Gym Reviews ("Sit down with your chest pressed against the seatback") — a qualitative setup fact, not a numeric one this research can cite, so it is not written into `machine.settings`
